chunks: And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Fasting is by the sighting [of the moon], and breaking the fast is by the sighting [of the moon], and the sighting is not valid if it is seen by one person, nor two, nor fifty."
And from him, from Al-Hasan, from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwah, from Abu Al-Abbas, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"Fasting is by the sighting [of the moon], and breaking the fast is by the sighting [of the moon], and the sighting is not valid if it is seen by one person, nor two, nor fifty."
ai.seo_question: What constitutes valid moon sighting for Ramadan fasting according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In Shia jurisprudence, this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the mere visual sighting of the crescent by individuals or small groups does not automatically establish the start or end of Ramadan, distinguishing between personal observation and legally binding communal testimony. This ruling underscores the necessity of widespread, verified confirmation (*tawatur*) or authoritative judicial declaration to ensure uniformity in the community's worship. It reflects the scholarly emphasis on preventing arbitrary changes to the lunar calendar based on isolated reports.
